title: Generic fields and component orbits in a finite quotient of a normal scheme
statement: Let $X$ and $Z$ be normal Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains and Noetherian means a finite affine cover by Noetherian rings. Let a finite group $H$ act on $X$, and let $q:X\to Z$ be an invariant finite surjective morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism] whose geometric fibres are $H$-orbits and whose structure sheaf satisfies $\mathcal O_Z=(q_*\mathcal O_X)^H$. Then $q$ maps generic points of $X$ to generic points of $Z$, and induces a bijection from $H$-orbits of irreducible components of $X$ to irreducible components of $Z$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-sc-generic-point]. If $\eta$ is a generic point of $X$, $\xi=q(\eta)$, $M=\kappa(\eta)$ and $D=\{h\in H:h\eta=\eta\}$, the canonical residue-field embedding identifies $\kappa(\xi)$ with $M^D=\{a\in M:ha=a\text{ for every }h\in D\}$ [def-weil-residue-field]. The action of $D$ on $M$ need not be faithful. In particular, the assertion applies to disconnected $X$ without a generically free action.

source.place: Agent-formulated generic-localization consequence of Tag 03BK (lemma-invariants-base-change), part (3), for the finite constant action groupoid: localization to a generic point commutes with invariants, and invariants of a transitively permuted product of fields identify with the fixed field of a factor stabilizer. Used in ILO X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.151, but no freeness or integral-source assumption is made here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space] to the finitely many affine opens in the Noetherian hypothesis on each of $X,Z$. A descending chain of closed subsets restricts to a stabilizing chain on each such open; the maximum of the finitely many stabilization indices works on their union. Thus both underlying spaces are Noetherian. Apply [lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components] to obtain finite, disjoint, clopen normal integral components $X_i$ and $Z_j$. The hypotheses on local rings are exactly the normality hypotheses of that node. The empty case has no components and the assertions are vacuous.

On an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $Z$, finiteness [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] gives $q^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Invariance of $q$ makes this open $H$-stable, and the assumed sheaf equality identifies the actual map $A\to B$ with the inclusion $B^H\subset B$. Apply [lem-a1-affine-groupoid-orbit-fibres] to the constant action groupoid $R=\coprod_{h\in H}\operatorname{Spec}B$: its affine presentation is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], source is the identity on each copy, and target is the action automorphism on that copy. Both maps are finite locally free: the source algebra is $\prod_{h\in H}B$, free over $B$ with its standard coordinate basis; the target is conjugate to this source projection by the automorphism $(h,x)\mapsto(h,hx)$. Its invariant ring is exactly $B^H$ . The groupoid identities are the action identities. The cited node therefore says that two points over $V$ have the same image exactly when one is an $H$-translate of the other. Since any common image lies in an affine open, this holds on all of $X$.

source.place: Tag 03BL (lemma-points), applied to the finite constant action groupoid.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], $q$ is closed. The group permutes the components $X_i$, since its maps are homeomorphisms. For a component orbit $O$, put $T_O=\bigcup_{i\in O}X_i$. It and its complement are closed. The point-orbit assertion of Step 2 gives $q^{-1}(q(T_O))=T_O$; surjectivity then gives $Z\setminus q(T_O)=q(X\setminus T_O)$. Hence $q(T_O)$ is clopen. For $i\in O$, invariance gives $q(T_O)=q(X_i)$, an irreducible nonempty subset: if its image lay in a union of two closed subsets, their inverse images would cover $X_i$, forcing one to contain it. Thus $q(T_O)$ is a nonempty irreducible clopen subset. By the disjoint integral component decomposition of $Z$ from Step 1 it is precisely one component $Z_j$. The sets $q(T_O)$ are disjoint by saturation and cover $Z$ by surjectivity, proving the desired component-orbit bijection.

source.place: Tag 01WN (lemma-finite-proper), followed by the elementary quotient-topology argument.

proof.text: Let $\eta_i$ be the generic point of $X_i$, whose existence and uniqueness follow from [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Continuity gives $q(X_i)=q(\overline{\{\eta_i\}})\subseteq\overline{\{q(\eta_i)\}}$. The reverse inclusion holds because $q(X_i)$ is closed and contains $q(\eta_i)$. By Step 3 this closed image is $Z_j$, so $q(\eta_i)$ is its generic point $\xi_j$. A group element fixes $\eta_i$ exactly when it stabilizes $X_i$: take closures for one implication, and uniqueness of its generic point for the other. Thus the stabilizer of this factor is exactly the group $D$ in the statement.

source.place: Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober), and continuity plus the closedness already proved in Step 3.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and $j$ as above and choose a nonempty affine open $V\subset Z_j$. Since $Z_j$ is open in $Z$, this is also an affine open of $Z$. Put $W=q^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$, using [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Each $W_k=X_k\cap W$, for $k\in O$, is clopen in $W$ and is nonempty because $q(X_k)=Z_j$. There are no other components meeting $W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] it is $D(e_k)$ for an idempotent of $B$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], part (b), it is affine. It is an open subscheme of the integral $X_k$. In fact its coordinate ring $B_k=\Gamma(W_k,\mathcal O_X)$ is a domain by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], applied to $X_k$. Sheaf gluing on the disjoint open cover $(W_k)_{k\in O}$ gives the actual restriction isomorphism $B\cong\prod_{k\in O}B_k$: a tuple of sections glues uniquely since all intersections are empty. This isomorphism intertwines the $H$-action, which sends the factor $B_k$ to $B_{hk}$ by inverse pullback.

Write $h:B_k\to B_{hk}$ for the inverse-pullback action. Projection to factor $i$ identifies $(\prod_{k\in O}B_k)^H$ with $B_i^D$. Explicitly an invariant tuple satisfies $b_{hi}=h(b_i)$, so its $i$th entry is fixed by $D$, and it is determined by that entry. Conversely for $a\in B_i^D$ set $b_{hi}=h(a)$. If $hi=h\prime i$, then $h^{-1}h\prime\in D$, so the entries agree; moreover $b_{ghi}=g(b_{hi})$, proving invariance. The inverse and projection preserve addition, multiplication and $1$ coordinatewise. Combining this with $A=B^H$ from the sheaf hypothesis gives an injective map $A\to B_i$ whose image is exactly $B_i^D$. It is the actual restriction of $q^\sharp$ to $W_i$, not an unspecified isomorphism.

source.place: Agent calculation for a transitively permuted finite product; the invariant-ring setup is that of Tag 03BK (lemma-invariants-base-change).

proof.text: By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] applied to the integral components $Z_j,X_i$ and their nonempty affine opens $V,W_i$, the generic stalks are respectively $\operatorname{Frac}A$ and $\operatorname{Frac}B_i$. A field has zero maximal ideal, so [def-weil-residue-field] identifies these stalks with $\kappa(\xi_j)$ and $M=\kappa(\eta_i)$. By [def-weil-open-immersion], restricting to these open components does not change the stalks or residue fields. The map $\kappa(\xi_j)\to M$ is the extension of $A\to B_i$ from Step 6: both send a section to its germ at the indicated generic point, and functoriality of germs makes that square commute. Its extension to fractions is unique because each nonzero denominator becomes a unit. The action of $D$ on $M$ similarly extends its action on $B_i$.

source.place: Tag 01RV (lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions), with the affine generic stalk calculation of Schemes Tag 01HV.

proof.text: The image of $\operatorname{Frac}A$ in $M=\operatorname{Frac}B_i$ is fixed by $D$, by Step 6. Conversely let $x=b/c\in M$ be fixed by $D$, with $b,c\in B_i$ and $c\ne0$. Set $d=\prod_{g\in D}g(c)$. This lies in $B_i^D$ and is nonzero because $B_i$ is a domain. Also $xd=b\prod_{g\in D,\,g\ne1}g(c)$ belongs to $B_i$, and $g(xd)=g(x)g(d)=xd$ for every $g\in D$. Thus both $d$ and $xd$ belong to $B_i^D$, the image of $A$, so $x=(xd)/d$ lies in the image of $\operatorname{Frac}A$. This proves $\kappa(\xi_j)=M^D$ through the canonical embedding of Step 7. The calculation uses finiteness but never faithfulness, never division by $|D|$, and it was carried out on an arbitrary component orbit; it therefore covers disconnected schemes, nonfree generic actions and arbitrary characteristic.
